- Public Law 118-31, 118th Congress; H.R. 2670; enacted **Dec. 22, 2023**.
- Cite as "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024."

## Sec. 2 — Organization
- Act organized into **seven divisions** (A–G): DoD Authorizations; Military Construction; DOE National Security; Funding Tables; Other Matters; Department of State Authorization Act of 2023; Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2024.
- Establishes full table of contents.

## Sec. 3 — Congressional Defense Committees
- (10 USC 101 note.) "Congressional defense committees" defined per 10 U.S.C. §101(a)(16).

## Sec. 4 — Budgetary Effects
- PAYGO effects (Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010) determined by reference to latest "Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation" statement jointly submitted by House/Senate Budget Committee Chairmen, if submitted prior to passage vote.

# Working Notes: NDAA FY2024 — Procurement & RDT&E Provisions (Secs. 123–243)

## PROCUREMENT (Title I)

**Sec. 123 — Multiyear Procurement, Virginia Class Submarines**
- Navy may enter ≥1 multiyear contracts for ≤13 Virginia class subs; subject to 10 USC 3501.
- Advance procurement authorized beginning FY2024 (long lead material; economic order quantities when cost savings achievable).
- Out-year payments (post-FY2025) subject to appropriations availability.
- Contracts must include termination-liability clause; US max liability = amount appropriated for the subs regardless of amount obligated.
- "Virginia class submarine" = Block VI configured.

**Sec. 124 — Auxiliary Personnel Lighter Program**
- Navy may contract (from FY2024) for ≤6 Auxiliary Personnel Lighter vessels + material.
- Payments subject to appropriations; termination liability limited to funding obligated at time of termination.

**Sec. 125 — V-22 Nacelle Improvement Program**
- SecDef must upgrade ≥24 V-22 aircraft per FY2024 budget plan.
- Exception: may reduce below 24 with certification to congressional defense committees that reduction serves national security.

**Sec. 126 — Government-Operated Dry Docks (San Diego, CA)**
- Navy solicitations for private-sector non-nuclear surface ship maintenance in San Diego may include Gov-operated dry docks only if insufficient private capacity (per 10 USC 2466).
- Applies to solicitations issued after enactment; terminates 5 years after enactment.

**Sec. 127 — Annual Reports on Government Docks**
- Navy report due June 30, 2024, annually through 2028: identifies each instance Gov dock used when private capacity sufficient + explanation.

## Subtitle D — Air Force Programs

**Sec. 131 — F-15 Retirement Limitation** (amends 10 USC 9062, adds subsec. (l))
- From enactment through Sept 30, 2029, Air Force may not: retire >68 F-15E; reduce funding for retained F-15E personnel/sustainment presuming future divest authority; keep F-15E in "XJ" excess status.
- Exception: case-by-case aircraft no longer mission capable/uneconomical to repair.
- Amends Sec. 150 of FY2023 NDAA (PL 117-263): adds subparagraph (E) requiring per-aircraft description of upgrades/modifications (date, cost) + estimated remaining service-life; adds annual updates due Oct 1, 2024–2029.
- Retirement authority under (l)(1)(A) not applicable until Sec. 150 requirements met.

**Sec. 132 — RQ-4 Aircraft** (amends 10 USC 9062, adds subsec. (m))
- From enactment through Sept 30, 2028: may not retire RQ-4; reduce funding presuming divest authority; keep in "XJ" status; or decrease total RQ-4 inventory below 10.
- Same case-by-case exception.

**Sec. 133 — Temporary Fighter Inventory Exception**
- Notwithstanding 10 USC 9062(i)(1), during covered period AF may decrease fighter primary mission aircraft inventory to ≥1,112.
- Covered period: enactment to Oct 1, 2024; thereafter 9062(i)(1) minimums reapply.
